\\n\\ud83d\\udcdd Walkthrough\\n\\n## Walkthrough\\n\\nAdds combo rarity, unlock cost, and level progression to combos; new ScriptableObjects and editor tooling for rarity data; Memory gains unlock/level persistence helpers; UI updated to render locked/special combos via a new SpecialComboCell and rarity visuals.\\n\\n## Changes\\n\\n|Cohort / File(s)|Summary|\\n|---|---|\\n|**Core Combo Definition**
`Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/ComboDefinition.cs`|Added `ERarityEnum` (Common, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic), `UnlockCost`, `Rarity`, `LevelMultipliers`, and computed properties `Locked`, `Level`, `MaxLevel` backed by `Memory` helpers.|\\n|**Rarity Data Infrastructure**
`Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/ComboRarityData.cs`, `Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/ComboRarityDefinition.cs`, `Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/ComboCellRarityData.cs`|New ScriptableObjects: `ComboRarityData` (singleton, editor FillComboRarities), `ComboRarityDefinition` (level requirements), and `CombosCellRarityData`/`ComboCellRarityData` (rarity display data and reset on load).|\\n|**Memory Persistence**
`Assets/Scripts/Helper/Memory.cs`|Added `IsComboUnlocked`, `UnlockCombo`, `GetComboLevel`, and `IncreaseComboLevel` to persist and query combo unlock state and levels.|\\n|**UI & Cells**
`Assets/Scripts/UI/ComboScreen.cs`, `Assets/Scripts/UI/SpecialComboCell.cs`|`ComboScreen` conditionally instantiates a `SpecialComboCell` for locked or non-Common combos; `LockedComboCell` renamed/refactored to `SpecialComboCell`, uses a `SerializedDictionary` for visuals, handles unlock flow and currency updates.|\\n|**Assets / Meta**
`Assets/Resources/Combos/*`, `Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/*.meta`, `Assets/Resources/Combos/*.asset.meta`, `Assets/Art/Textures/UI/*.meta`|Added folder/meta entries and asset meta files for rarity assets and new scriptable object meta files; new texture meta entries for rare backgrounds/frames.|\\n\\n## Sequence Diagram\\n\\n```mermaid\\nsequenceDiagram\\n participant ComboScreen as ComboScreen\\n participant ComboDefinition as ComboDefinition\\n participant Memory as Memory\\n participant SpecialComboCell as SpecialComboCell\\n participant RarityData as CombosCellRarityData\\n\\n ComboScreen->>ComboDefinition: read Locked, Rarity\\n ComboDefinition->>Memory: IsComboUnlocked(name)\\n Memory-->>ComboDefinition: unlocked/locked\\n\\n alt Locked or Rarity != Common\\n ComboScreen->>SpecialComboCell: Instantiate _specialPrefab\\n SpecialComboCell->>ComboDefinition: evaluate Locked\\n alt Locked\\n SpecialComboCell->>RarityData: request visuals for Rarity\\n RarityData-->>SpecialComboCell: return sprites/text\\n SpecialComboCell->>Memory: UnlockCombo(name) [on user action]\\n Memory-->>SpecialComboCell: persist result\\n else Unlocked (special)\\n SpecialComboCell->>RarityData: request visuals for Rarity\\n RarityData-->>SpecialComboCell: return sprites/text\\n end\\n else Common & Unlocked\\n ComboScreen->>ComboScreen: Instantiate regular cell and add to list\\n end\\n```\\n\\n## Estimated Code Review Effort\\n\\n\\ud83c\\udfaf 3 (Moderate) | \\u23f1\\ufe0f ~22 minutes\\n\\n## Poem\\n\\n> \\ud83d\\udc30 I munched the code in twilight's glow, \\n> > Rarities shimmer, seeds now sow, \\n> > Locks click open with a little clack, \\n> > Multipliers hop the damage track, \\n> > A rabbit cheers \\u2014 combos on the go!\\n\\n

Critical finding on **#37**: the final merged `ComboDefinition.cs` shows Oliver's requested changes *were actually applied* — enum renamed to `ERarityEnum`, the `Locked` field removed and replaced with a computed `IsLocked => !ComboManager.Instance.IsComboUnlocked(Id)`, and `LevelMultiplierRow` gone. So the code got fixed even though no formal approval was ever recorded. Notably, the enum shipped as **4 tiers (Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic)** — `Common` was removed before merge.

Let me pull Oliver's actual review comments on #35, read the combo design docs, and verify #26's shipped code.

content.content: {"result":"{\"mimeType\": \"text/markdown\", \"text\": \"Overview\\n\\n### 1. Game Overview\\nTitle: Combo Fighter\\nGenre: Merge puzzle auto battler\\nPlatform: (iOS / Android)\\nCore Loop Summary:\\nPlace fight-action tetris shaped pieces on a game board and watch the character fight hordes of enemies.\\n### 2. Core Gameplay\\nPlayer Actions:\\nDrag tetris shaped pieces onto the game board, merge pieces to upgrade them, connect the pieces to create combos to deal extra damage, fill the board with more pieces to deal more attacks and/or damage.\\nDraw additional pieces randomly to place them on the board. Optimize your spaces and combo connections.\\nGain experience by defeating monsters and merging tiles. Experience levels up the hero and the player can choose a skill upgrade.\\nWhen the game ends, the player can upgrade the hero's Max HP, HP regen rate during the game, and attack power.\\nGame Objective:\\nDefeat all the waves of monsters in each level.\\nFailure Condition:\\nThe player\\u2019s HP reaches 0 from monster attacks.\\n### 3. Game Flow\\nHome Screen: Start button, current level displayed, three upgrade buttons.\\nGameplay: 4 to 5 minutes per level. The game switches from preparation phase to battle phase with occasional pop up dialogue for roguelite skill upgrades.\\nResult Screen: Displays rewards earned. Gold only in MVP.\\nUpgrades: Hero\\u2019s Max HP, HP regen rate, hero\\u2019s attack power bonus\\n### 4. Level Design\\n35 hand crafted levels in MVP\\nMonsters will have increased HP and attack damage as level progresses.\\nLevels will have obstacles on the board to create difficulty. These obstacles can be removed with silver earned in the level. These obstacles reset each game.\\nLevels will have different starting points for first combo piece placement. Each level will also have a set of possible pieces that can be dropped and their drop rate.\\n### 5. Art & Visual Style\\nThe top portion of the screen is dedicated to combat visualization during battle phase, the bottom portion only displays the puzzle board.\\nDuring intermission between waves of monsters, the camera shifts down to reveal a puzzle board + three slots staging area for players to obtain new puzzle pieces, this is the preparation phase. Pressing a FIGHT button will shift the camera back up and transition into the battle phase.\\nCharacter Designs: Simple Chibi style 3D characters.\\nUI: Simple standard UI, home screen with minimal buttons.\\n### 6. Audio\\nMusic: None\\nSFX: Standard fighting sounds.\\n### 7. Monetization\\nAds: None in MVP\\n### 8. Ugly Game Mockups\\nHome Screen with 3 upgrade choices, start button, coin balance and settings button\\n\\nGameplay\\n\\nGame Starts, 3 pieces randomly selected for players to choose from.\\nPlayers drag pieces onto the board, the character starts doing loop animation of the attacks on the board.\\nThe values showing total punch, kick and special attack power changes real time based on pieces on the board\\nThe dmg/s calculation also updates real time as pieces are being placed\\nThe Info button will bring up a pop up of available moves (see below)\\nPressing refresh will consume gold if available, and refreshes the 3 cards.\\nHolding a tile under the finger will change the refresh button to SELL. If a player moves pieces over the sell button, the piece will be sold.\\nCoin balance and health is displayed near the top\\nAfter pressing the fight button, the camera shifts upward to increase the size of the fight scene and the battle starts. This phase requires no input action from the players\\nInfo Pop Up\\n\\nSimple End Game Screen\\n\\n\\nDOCUMENT DOES NOT END HERE! MAKE SURE TO CLICK ON THE OTHER TABS (\\u201cDetailed Mechanics\\u201d) IN THIS DOCUMENT ON THE LEFT SIDE BAR IN GOOGLE DOCS\\n\\n\\nDetailed Mechanics\\n### 1. Starting A Level\\nLevel starts with a 6x6 empty game board.\\nThe level designer will indicate which left most square tile will be the first tile that starts the combo, if tiles are not placed here, There are no combos and only Singular attacks.\\n\\nPlayers are presented with a staging area with 3 random tiles at start. They can use these tiles on their board or sell them, or they can press the refresh button which costs silver to be dealt three more random tiles. Pressing the fight buttons begins the battle phase. The tiles themselves are free, only refresh costs money.\\n\\nTiles that remain on the board when the refresh button is pressed are sold automatically for 10 gold each.\\nOnce the battle phase starts, the character automatically executes the fighting sequence based on the tiles placed. The enemies will approach from the right side of the screen. If combos are not present on the board, then the player will perform one attack each of punch and/or kicks and/or special attacks if those action tiles exist. There is a 0.6 seconds delay between these attack animations, and these tiles that are not part of the combo will have an attack power penalty. So for example if a combo does not exist, but There are P K and S tiles on the board, the player will do Punch (basic jab animation) \\u2192 0.6 second delay \\u2192 Kick (basic roundhouse kick animation) \\u2192 0.6 second delay \\u2192 Special attack (fireball) \\u2192 0.6 second delay \\u2192 repeat\\n\\nWhen the monster crosses the green line seen below, the character will automatically execute the fighting combo. When the monster crosses the red line, they will start to attack the player.\\n\\nIf There are no monsters within melee range of the player, the player will execute a ranged attack based on the total special attack power, with a 0.8 seconds delay between each attack. (Fireball Hadouken animation)\\n\\nFireball will hit 3 enemies before disappearing. This can be upgraded. So in this case we can upgrade a fireball to hit the left most 6 enemies.\\nPlayers will gain experience and silver from killing monsters. Experience will allow the player to level up within the game and select some random upgrades. Silver is used to obtain more tiles during the preparation phase.\\n\\nWhen the wave of monsters is defeated, the camera shifts back down exposing the staging area and we are back to the preparation phase where players get to acquire more tiles and optimize their placements on the board. The game ends in a loss if the player is defeated and HP reaches 0.\\nThe game ends in victory if the player defeats all waves of monsters.\\nPLEASE NOTE THAT THE AMOUNT OF SILVER AND EXP RECEIVED IS NOT BASED ON MONSTER TYPE KILLED OR QUANTITY OF MONSTERS KILLED. Instead, we are introducing a system that allows designers to set the amount of exp and silver a player will receive each wave, and we divide that across the monsters in that wave..\\n\\n#### Block Merging & Rearrangement\\nWhen the preparation phase starts, There will be 3 blocks spawned in the bottom area to place or merge.\\nHolding a piece will show possible placements with highlighted corners.\\nWhen the tiles have mergeable counterparts in the board, the mergeable tile on the board will have a glowing outline.\\nLike the video below.\\nScreenRecording_11-11-2025 16-11-07_1.MP4\\nWhile arranging the placement of blocks, players can move board tiles to the bottom area and rearrange them back and forth.\\nThe only limitation is that 3 blocks can be stored on the bottom part.\\nOnce players decide to continue fighting, clicking the \\u201cFight\\u201d button, the pieces left on the bottom would be sold automatically.\\nPlayers can merge the blocks in the bottom part.\\n### 2. Combat Power and Damage Calculation\\nThere are three types of action tiles: Punch (P), Kick (K) and Special Attack (S). The corresponding tile colors are green, blue, and red.\\n\\nTiles will display the full combat power they provide. Not penalized discounted power.\\n\\nTiles will come in different shapes\\n\\nPunch has a base attack power of 10, Kick is 20, and Special Attack is 40\\n\\nThe same tiles can be merged and upgraded to increase their power. Tiles that are not part of a combo and only contribute half power are called \\u201cAssist Tiles,\\u201d they are dimmed visually. When merged it simply sums the combat power. So level 1 Punch = 10, level 2 punch = 20, level 3 punch = 40 (Requires 2x level 2) They do not need to be connected to any pieces to contribute. They just need to be on the board.\\n\\nThe individual power of the combo is shown in the UI like seen here below.\\n\\n\\n\\nThe damage per attack sequence is based on the only combo on the board, each board can only have a max of one combo, and for each action in the combo, the damage dealt is calculated using the following:\\n\\n[Action Power] = [Tile Power + (50%*(SUM of assist tile power))] * Combo Bonus Multiplier\\nThis calculates the individual action power for the combo\\n\\nCombo multipliers are pre-assigned by game designers. Here is an example of a combo calculation.\\n\\n\\n\\nSmall sample list of combos and their multiplier and base DPS, this is accessed via the info button during the game. The character at the top animates the combo punching air/dummy when the player selects a combo.\\n\\n\\n\\n### 3. Combo Creation UI/UX\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n### 4. Game Currencies and Homescreen Upgrades\\nThere will be 3 different upgradeable stats at the home screen which are persistent across sessions and levels. The currency used to upgrade is gold. We can consider adding an ad watch when players run out of gold.\\nThey will be extended with gears or other upgrades that we can use later on. So for the implementation, please be aware that we can extend upgrades.\\nAttack Increase (+2% per upgrade. Additive) So 100% + 2% + 2% + 2% + 2% (Level 4 = 108% * attack)\\nHealth Increase (+2% per upgrade. Additive) Same as attack. So level 5 health increase = 110% * base HP of 100 = 110 total Hp\\nHealth Regen Increase (+0.02% per second, Additive) So level 7 is 2% base regen + (0.02% * 7 = 0.14%) final health regen = 2.14% HP regen per second.\\n### 5. Monsters, Stats, Damage Assignment, Stagger and Loot\\nEach monster when hit is \\u201cstunned\\u201d for 0.25 seconds. However this has a cooldown of 1.5 seconds. This means after being stunned, the earliest the next time the same monster can be stunned again is 1.25 seconds later because 1.5 second cooldown from first stun - 0.25 stun duration = 1.25 seconds after end of first stun.\\nMonster attack animation should be from start to finish should be 1 second, with damage dealt at 0.8 second timestamp\\nWe do not need more than 5 monsters for MVP\\nWhen monsters are hit, we display damage dealt using standard RPG text VFX. We then display the monster health bar permanently above their head, but we do not display numerical values for their HP\\nMonster speed is the second it takes to move from edge of screen to crossing the monster attack line. Attack speed is expressed in seconds per attack.\\n\\n\\n### 6. Levels\\nWe need to let designers designate starting positions for each level.\\nEach level will also have obstacles that need to be removed via silver.\\n\\nEach level will have 15 waves of monsters\\nEach wave of monsters will get an HP and damage multiplier bonus following a standard algorithm\\nHP multiplier for monster is wave # * XXX\\nDamage multiplier for monster is wave # * YYY\\nWe need to utilize the monster spawning system from Zombie Match, this will allow designers to specify monsters spawn timing and quantity\\n#### Level Design Tools\\nEach level will have monsters, monsters spawn, their stats, board type, and the pool of tiles available.\\nSo what\\u2019s needed from a level is that\\nLEVEL NAME\\nMonster Track\\nWaves\\nMonster type,\\nMonster amount,\\nSpawn Duration (fixed or interval)\\n[USERNAME_5859]\\u2019s stats (dmg & HP)\\nWave multiplier for damage & HP (separate)\\nAnother wave\\nMonster type,\\nMonster amount,\\nSpawn Duration (fixed or interval)\\n[USERNAME_5859]\\u2019s stats (dmg & HP)\\nWave multiplier for damage & HP (separate)\\nBoard Info\\nPool of tiles\\nAbility to select available tiles used in that level\\nSpawn rate of individual tiles\\nSpawn rate of colors (?)\\nSpawn rate of shapes (?)\\nPool types (if necessary later on)\\nStart and exit nodes  (if necessary later on)\\n### 7. Player Starting Stats\\nBase player HP is 100\\nBase player regen rate is 2% per second, but this is only during the \\u201cfight\\u201d phase and not the prep phase.\\nBase attack is 0, no tiles placed = no damage.\\n\\n### 8. ### 1. Game Overview
Title: Combo Fighter
Genre: Merge puzzle auto battler
Platform: (iOS / Android)
Core Loop Summary:
Place fight-action tetris shaped pieces on a game board and watch the character fight hordes of enemies.
### 2. Core Gameplay
Player Actions:
Drag tetris shaped pieces onto the game board, merge pieces to upgrade them, connect the pieces to create combos to deal extra damage, fill the board with more pieces to deal more attacks and/or damage.
Draw additional pieces randomly to place them on the board. Optimize your spaces and combo connections.
Gain experience by defeating monsters and merging tiles. Experience levels up the hero and the player can choose a skill upgrade.

Game Objective:
Defeat all the waves of monsters in each level.
Failure Condition:
The player’s HP reaches 0 from monster attacks.
### 3. Game Flow
Home Screen: Start button, current level displayed, three upgrade buttons.
Gameplay: 4 to 5 minutes per level. The game switches from preparation phase to battle phase with occasional pop up dialogue for roguelite skill upgrades.
Result Screen: Displays rewards earned. Gold only in MVP.

35 hand crafted levels in MVP

Music: None

Detailed Mechanics
### 1. Starting A Level
Level starts with a 6x6 empty game board.
The level designer will indicate which left most square tile will be the first tile that starts the combo, if tiles are not placed here, There are no combos and only Singular attacks.

Players are presented with a staging area with 3 random tiles at start. They can use these tiles on their board or sell them, or they can press the refresh button which costs silver to be dealt three more random tiles. Pressing the fight buttons begins the battle phase. The tiles themselves are free, only refresh costs money.

Tiles that remain on the board when the refresh button is pressed are sold automatically for 10 gold each.
Once the battle phase starts, the character automatically executes the fighting sequence based on the tiles placed. The enemies will approach from the right side of the screen. If combos are not present on the board, then the player will perform one attack each of punch and/or kicks and/or special attacks if those action tiles exist. There is a 0.6 seconds delay between these attack animations, and these tiles that are not part of the combo will have an attack power penalty. So for example if a combo does not exist, but There are P K and S tiles on the board, the player will do Punch (basic jab animation) → 0.6 second delay → Kick (basic roundhouse kick animation) → 0.6 second delay → Special attack (fireball) → 0.6 second delay → repeat

When the monster crosses the green line seen below, the character will automatically execute the fighting combo. When the monster crosses the red line, they will start to attack the player.

If There are no monsters within melee range of the player, the player will execute a ranged attack based on the total special attack power, with a 0.8 seconds delay between each attack. (Fireball Hadouken animation)

Fireball will hit 3 enemies before disappearing. This can be upgraded. So in this case we can upgrade a fireball to hit the left most 6 enemies.
Players will gain experience and silver from killing monsters. Experience will allow the player to level up within the game and select some random upgrades. Silver is used to obtain more tiles during the preparation phase.

When the wave of monsters is defeated, the camera shifts back down exposing the staging area and we are back to the preparation phase where players get to acquire more tiles and optimize their placements on the board. The game ends in a loss if the player is defeated and HP reaches 0.
The game ends in victory if the player defeats all waves of monsters.
PLEASE NOTE THAT THE AMOUNT OF SILVER AND EXP RECEIVED IS NOT BASED ON MONSTER TYPE KILLED OR QUANTITY OF MONSTERS KILLED. Instead, we are introducing a system that allows designers to set the amount of exp and silver a player will receive each wave, and we divide that across the monsters in that wave..

#### Block Merging & Rearrangement
When the preparation phase starts, There will be 3 blocks spawned in the bottom area to place or merge.
Holding a piece will show possible placements with highlighted corners.
When the tiles have mergeable counterparts in the board, the mergeable tile on the board will have a glowing outline.
Like the video below.
ScreenRecording_11-11-2025 16-11-07_1.MP4
While arranging the placement of blocks, players can move board tiles to the bottom area and rearrange them back and forth.
The only limitation is that 3 blocks can be stored on the bottom part.
Once players decide to continue fighting, clicking the “Fight” button, the pieces left on the bottom would be sold automatically.
Players can merge the blocks in the bottom part.
### 2. Combat Power and Damage Calculation
There are three types of action tiles: Punch (P), Kick (K) and Special Attack (S). The corresponding tile colors are green, blue, and red.

Tiles will display the full combat power they provide. Not penalized discounted power.

Tiles will come in different shapes

Punch has a base attack power of 10, Kick is 20, and Special Attack is 40

The same tiles can be merged and upgraded to increase their power. Tiles that are not part of a combo and only contribute half power are called “Assist Tiles,” they are dimmed visually. When merged it simply sums the combat power. So level 1 Punch = 10, level 2 punch = 20, level 3 punch = 40 (Requires 2x level 2) They do not need to be connected to any pieces to contribute. They just need to be on the board.

The individual power of the combo is shown in the UI like seen here below.



The damage per attack sequence is based on the only combo on the board, each board can only have a max of one combo, and for each action in the combo, the damage dealt is calculated using the following:

[Action Power] = [Tile Power + (50%*(SUM of assist tile power))] * Combo Bonus Multiplier
This calculates the individual action power for the combo

Combo multipliers are pre-assigned by game designers. Here is an example of a combo calculation.



Small sample list of combos and their multiplier and base DPS, this is accessed via the info button during the game. The character at the top animates the combo punching air/dummy when the player selects a combo.



### 3. Combo Creation UI/UX




### 4. Game Currencies and Homescreen Upgrades
There will be 3 different upgradeable stats at the home screen which are persistent across sessions and levels. The currency used to upgrade is gold. We can consider adding an ad watch when players run out of gold.
They will be extended with gears or other upgrades that we can use later on. So for the implementation, please be aware that we can extend upgrades.
Attack Increase (+2% per upgrade. Additive) So 100% + 2% + 2% + 2% + 2% (Level 4 = 108% * attack)
Health Increase (+2% per upgrade. Additive) Same as attack. So level 5 health increase = 110% * base HP of 100 = 110 total Hp
Health Regen Increase (+0.02% per second, Additive) So level 7 is 2% base regen + (0.02% * 7 = 0.14%) final health regen = 2.14% HP regen per second.
### 5. Monsters, Stats, Damage Assignment, Stagger and Loot
Each monster when hit is “stunned” for 0.25 seconds. However this has a cooldown of 1.5 seconds. This means after being stunned, the earliest the next time the same monster can be stunned again is 1.25 seconds later because 1.5 second cooldown from first stun - 0.25 stun duration = 1.25 seconds after end of first stun.
Monster attack animation should be from start to finish should be 1 second, with damage dealt at 0.8 second timestamp
We do not need more than 5 monsters for MVP
When monsters are hit, we display damage dealt using standard RPG text VFX. We then display the monster health bar permanently above their head, but we do not display numerical values for their HP
Monster speed is the second it takes to move from edge of screen to crossing the monster attack line. Attack speed is expressed in seconds per attack.


### 6. Levels
We need to let designers designate starting positions for each level.
Each level will also have obstacles that need to be removed via silver.

Each level will have 15 waves of monsters
Each wave of monsters will get an HP and damage multiplier bonus following a standard algorithm
HP multiplier for monster is wave # * XXX
Damage multiplier for monster is wave # * YYY
We need to utilize the monster spawning system from Zombie Match, this will allow designers to specify monsters spawn timing and quantity

input.title: Combo-Fighters PR #35 merged over standing CHANGES_REQUESTED — auth tokens logged in prod
input.description:
Record of review state at the Feb-2026 freeze (Combo Fighter is live/monetizing). Recording state only — not assigning.

**PR:** harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters #35 "Blake/backend" — author Arthur Blake (@EMPLOYEE_0025), merged by the author.
**Review:** Oliver Brooks left `CHANGES_REQUESTED` on 2026-01-30 20:36. Merged by Arthur ~57 min later (21:33) with **no approving review**. Sign-off never happened.

**What the reviewer / CodeRabbit pushed back on, and what actually landed on `main`:**
- ✅ Addressed: login GET now URL-encodes params via `Uri.EscapeDataString`; POST body JSON escaping added.
- ❌ NOT addressed (LIVE on main): `AWSGameSDKClient.SdkLoginCallback` writes the raw login response — which contains `auth_token`, `refresh_token`, and `guest_secret` — into `Debug.LogError` on any parse failure (both the credential sanity-check branch and the catch block: `...RawResponse:{rawResponse}`). Sensitive auth material lands in device logs.
- ❌ NOT addressed: `GetUserCountry()` calls `new RegionInfo(CultureInfo.CurrentCulture.Name)` with no guard — throws `ArgumentException` on neutral/invariant cultures.
- ❌ NOT addressed: authenticated GET `CallRestApiGetWithAuth` still concatenates params without URL-encoding (only the login GET was fixed).
- Oliver inline (`ProfileScreen.cs`): "Looks dangerous" — `_statPrefab` is a GameObject that is Instantiated then ignored if it lacks a `ProfileStat`; recommended typing the field as `ProfileStat`. Also "missing `private`". `Store/DominoPlayerPrefs.cs`: "Can we rename this?" — Arthur replied "Yes" but merged before confirming; other items got no sign-off.

**Category:** author engaged only minimally (two "Yes" replies); most points neither addressed nor signed off.

input.title: Combo-Fighters PR #26 merged over unresolved reviewer objection — ad-cooldown bypass is live
input.description:
Record of review state at the Feb-2026 freeze. Recording state only — not assigning.

**PR:** harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters #26 "Added cooldown to main menu upgrade ad watch" — author @PERSON_5877, merged by Oliver Brooks.
**Review:** Oliver Brooks left `CHANGES_REQUESTED` on 2026-01-15 13:36. Merged 2026-01-15 17:28 with **no approving review afterwards**.

**Substance — the objection that is still standing (and live on `main`):**
Oliver's review body: "I think we should try a solution that uses time... The problem with this solution is that the player can enter the level, lose very quickly and return to main menu and then they will be able to watch another ad and level up again." The shipped code does exactly this: the upgrade-ad cooldown is reset on level completion (`GameController.GameRoutine`) AND on loss (`LoseScreen`), so a player can bypass the cooldown by losing quickly. This weakens the ad-gate on a live/monetizing build. Not addressed before merge, no reviewer sign-off.

**Also unactioned:** Oliver's inline note to move the `Memory.SetUpgradeAdWatchedCooldown(reset:true)` / `AddGold` lines out of `GameController` into `WinScreen` — author never responded; still in `GameController`.
**Resolved during review (for completeness):** the `Memory.cs` "move to Memory" note was a reviewer mistake ("Ops, my bad").

**Category:** author engaged on a side point (deferred to Robert re: win/lose) but the core objection was neither resolved nor signed off.
**File(s):** `Assets/Scripts/Managers/GameController.cs`, `Assets/Scripts/UI/LoseScreen.cs`, `Assets/Scripts/Ads/UI/MainMenuAdsController.cs`, `Assets/Scripts/Helper/Memory.cs`.
**Status when everyone stopped:** merged with objection standing; exploit confirmed present on `main`.

input.title: Combo-Fighters PR #37 merged without formal sign-off (changes addressed in code, never re-approved) + combo rarity spec gap
input.description:
Record of review state at the Feb-2026 freeze. Recording state only — not assigning.

**PR:** harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters #37 "Combo Definition Updates" — author @PERSON_5877, merged by Oliver Brooks.
**Review:** Oliver Brooks left `CHANGES_REQUESTED` on 2026-02-12. Merged 2026-02-13 21:59 with **no subsequent approving review** — GitHub still shows it unresolved.

**BUT — what actually landed on the branch/`main` shows the concerns were addressed in code:**
- ✅ Enum renamed to `ERarityEnum` (the "start enums with E" request).
- ✅ `Locked` field removed from the ScriptableObject; now computed `IsLocked => !ComboManager.Instance.IsComboUnlocked(Id)` (reviewer's point: SO must not persist lock state — now backed by ComboManager/PlayerPrefs).
- ✅ `LevelMultiplierRow` helper class removed.
- ✅ Rarity display data consolidated into a `SerializedDictionary<ERarityEnum, ...>` (reviewer's refactor suggestion).
- On `_specialPrefab` naming (reviewer suggested `_lockedPrefab`), the author pushed back — "not only locked combos use this prefab" — and the reviewer's suggestion was consciously not taken.

**Category:** author came back and argued the point; code was fixed anyway. This one only *looks* unresolved on GitHub — the substance was resolved; only the formal re-approval is missing. Leave the code alone; this ticket exists so the next person can tell it apart from #26/#35.

**Design-spec gap (separate finding, Owen's ask):** the combo rarity/unlock/leveling system introduced here — `ERarityEnum {Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic}`, `UnlockCost = 300`, per-rarity `BonusIncreasePerLevel` — is NOT documented in the Combo Fighter GDD or the "Combo Fighter Design Details" sheet. The GDD's combo section (§9) is a placeholder; the "Combo List" tab only holds bonus-damage multipliers/DPS with no rarity, unlock cost, or level-up table. No "Combo Unlocking Specs" / rarity design doc exists in Drive or Docs — the spec cited in the PR review only ever lived in Slack (#prototype, 2026-02-12) and the PR comments. The tier set roughly matches the Slack decision (4 tiers, common = no label) but names/order differ ("Mythic" vs the Slack "Mythical"), and the per-rarity level-up value table the author described in review is not present in any design doc.

**File(s):** `Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/ComboDefinition.cs`, `ComboRarityData.cs`, `ComboRarityDefinition.cs`, `Assets/Scripts/UI/ComboScreen.cs`, `SpecialComboCell.cs`, `Assets/Scripts/Helper/Memory.cs`.
**Status when everyone stopped:** merged, resolved-in-code, no formal sign-off; rarity feature undocumented on the design side.

Arthur — Combo Fighter review-state audit, recorded before we lose tooling access. Went through every PR on `harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters` (37 total). Ground rules followed: comment left on each flagged PR, one ENG ticket per PR, all left unassigned.

*The rule:* a PR is only "clean" if the reviewer approved before it went in. I checked what actually landed on the branch after each objection — not just the review badge. Result: **3 PRs merged with a `CHANGES_REQUESTED` still standing and no later approval.** Everything else was either approved before merge (#24, #21, #16, #9 — process worked, left alone) or had no review objection at all.

*Reviewer on all three was Oliver Brooks. Here's the split you asked for:*

*① Objection still standing, and it's actually live — needs eyes*
• *PR #26 — ad-watch cooldown* (`GameController`/`LoseScreen`/`MainMenuAdsController`). Oliver said in review: a time-based cooldown that resets when the level ends lets a player "enter the level, lose very quickly and return to main menu and then watch another ad and level up again." The merged code resets the cooldown on both win *and* loss — so that exploit is exactly what shipped. Confirmed live on `main`. Author engaged on a side point (deferred to Robert on win/lose) but the core concern was never resolved or signed off. → *ENG-2439*
• *PR #35 — Blake/backend* (auth SDK). Your own PR, merged by you ~1h after Oliver's CHANGES_REQUESTED, no approval. Some review points *were* fixed (login GET now URL-encodes). But still live on `main`: `AWSGameSDKClient` logs the raw login response — which contains `auth_token`, `refresh_token`, `guest_secret` — to `Debug.LogError` on any parse error. Auth tokens in device logs on a paying build. Also `GetUserCountry()` can throw on some locales; `ProfileScreen` has an instantiate-and-ignore prefab pattern Oliver flagged as "dangerous." → *ENG-2438*

*② Reviewer was argued with, but the code got fixed anyway — looks unresolved, isn't*
• *PR #37 — Combo Definition Updates.* Standing CHANGES_REQUESTED, no re-approval, so GitHub shows it red. But the branch shows the author actually applied the fixes before merge: enum renamed to `ERarityEnum`, the `Locked` field pulled out of the ScriptableObject into `ComboManager`/PlayerPrefs, `LevelMultiplierRow` removed, rarity visuals moved to a SerializedDictionary. On the one point he pushed back (prefab naming) his rationale was sound and consciously kept. Substance is resolved; only the formal sign-off is missing. **Leave the code alone.** → *ENG-2440*

*On "agreed then never landed" (the worst kind):* I didn't find a clean case of someone saying yes and it vanishing. Closest is #35 — you replied "Yes" to renaming `DominoPlayerPrefs` then merged, and Oliver's `ProfileScreen` fixes were never signed off — but nothing that read as settled-and-then-dropped. Worth knowing that's *not* what's here.

*Design side (Owen's flag — "the spec I pointed at during a review may not say what I said"):* checked. The combo rarity/unlock/leveling system in #37 — `ERarityEnum {Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic}`, 300 unlock cost, per-rarity level bonus — is **not** in the GDD or the Combo Fighter Design Details sheet. The GDD's combo section is a placeholder; the "Combo List" tab only has bonus-damage multipliers/DPS, no rarity/unlock/level table. There's no "Combo Unlocking Specs" doc anywhere in Drive or Docs — the spec cited in that PR only ever existed in this channel (Feb 12) and the PR comments. Tiers roughly match what was decided here (4 kinds, common = no label), but the naming drifted ("Mythic" vs the "Mythical" we discussed) and the level-up value table the author described in review isn't written down anywhere. So: shipped feature, undocumented design — captured in ENG-2440.

Full detail (files, exact quotes, what did/didn't land) is in each ticket and on each PR.
